Repeatedly positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR (node-11), transient anosmia/ageusia (node-2), oral and genital erosions with truncal vesicles (node-4), and absence of precipitating medications (node-3) all support this specific diagnosis. Skin biopsy/DIF is still pending, so moderate confidence is appropriate.

payload.report: Repeatedly positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR confirms active COVID-19, and transient anosmia/ageusia supports a viral trigger. Negative Mycoplasma IgM and other respiratory pathogens, with no pre-eruption medications, argue against drug eruption, Mycoplasma-related EM, and other infections. Characteristic oral/genital erosions with truncal vesicles fit erythema multiforme, and pathologist analysis favors COVID-19-associated EM. Mycoplasma IgG elevation reflects past infection, not acute disease. Pending skin biopsy/DIF and HSV/VZV/enterovirus serology leave autoimmune bullous disease and HSV/Mycoplasma-related EM not fully excluded, but overall evidence best supports COVID-19-associated erythema multiforme.
